exposure: induction at 38 weeks for severe ICP
Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) management guidelines (induction at 38 weeks vs. induction at 38 weeks only for severe ICP)
cohort: 62,937 women with singleton deliveries at Rigshospitalet and 71,015 at Hvidovre Hospital in Copenhagen from 2004 to 2015, including 971 women (1.5%) and 998 women (1.4%) diagnosed with ICP, respectively
finding: Two different approaches to managing mild intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP), one with routine induction at 38 weeks and the other reserving induction for severe cases, showed comparable outcomes for both mothers and infants.
mod_finding: The study compared two guidelines for managing intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy, finding no difference in rates of spontaneous labor, cesarean section, or induction.
